$comment: Per-machine installer facts for Dyno (family ADR 0053 section 2.1 and 3). stopExclusions: programs of the bundle that stop-all must not end, each with a reason. survivesForcedEnd: the adoption's statement that every program in the stop list survives a forced end without losing more than its last unfinished write; each entry names what was checked.

stopExclusions.reason: The helper service runs from its own protected folder, Dyno Helper in Program Files, which an update or uninstall of the install folder must not touch. A dyno-helper.exe that runs from the install folder is an elevated install or removal of a few seconds, and ending it halfway could leave the service half registered. It is left alone and not reported: if it still runs when the files are replaced, the installer's file copy reports a locked file.

survivesForcedEnd.why: The app window keeps no data of its own; its settings are written by paddock-settings through a temporary file and a rename (crates/paddock-settings/src/file.rs:226), so a forced end leaves the old file whole.

The history store and the cache are SQLite in WAL mode with synchronous NORMAL (dyno-agent/src/store.rs:61-62, cache/db.rs:343-344): a forced end loses at most the last unflushed transactions and leaves a consistent database. Its other files are written to a temporary name, synced and renamed (dyno-agent/src/files.rs:25-36); discovery and instance files are hints that the next start rewrites (rule 53).
The command line client reads from the agent and writes nothing but its own output.
A benchmark run keeps its result in memory until it is finished; a forced end loses that run only, and its scratch files are removed by the next run (dyno-agent/src/bench_scratch.rs).
As dyno-bench.exe: the result is reported when the run ends; a forced end loses that run only.
